_note: Gameplay data (engine/player/items.h): the player's numbers, the clock, what a new game starts with and every item. Never in the golden hash. Foods follow Valheim: health and stamina raise the MAXIMUM of each while the food lasts (its value is (time left / duration)^food_decay_power of the full amounts), regen is health a tick (every regen_interval_s), duration_s is seconds of play, and a food can be eaten again once below food_refresh_at of its time. A tool's `tool` block is what it does to a creature and when: damage a hit, reach_m from the eye along the swing (engine/mobs/combat.h), and the swing's timing (engine/player/swing.h) -- impact_s after the press the blow LANDS, at the point in the animation where the head meets the wood, and recover_s after that the next swing may start. A click arriving inside a swing is kept if the swing is within the player block's swing_buffer_s of ending, and swung as it frees up. anim is the clip the upper body plays and anim_s how much of it (0 for all): the axe takes 0.78 s of UAL's 1.533 s Sword_Attack, whose strike runs 0.33-0.50 s and which holds a second swing after it. Icons are shapes in a unit square, y down, painted in order: e [cx, cy, rx, ry] an ellipse, r [x0, y0, x1, y1] a rectangle turned rot degrees, p [x, y, ...] a polygon; c #rrggbb[aa], sRGB.
_note_stealth: The player as creatures hear and see them (docs/adr-007-creatures-perception-navigation.md). Sound: dB at 1 m, heard at d metres as dB - 20 log10(d) against a creature's threshold within its range. Gaits by speed (walk 1.4 m/s, jog 5, sprint 8), silent standing; events are spikes decaying at spike_decay_db_s. Visibility 0..1 by posture and speed scales a creature's view range, and so does the light on the player, on a log scale from dark_lux (light_floor) to full_lux (1).
_note_clock: day_length_min: real minutes of play for 24 game hours. Forage regrows in game days (worldgen/data/archetypes.json forage regrow_days).
_note_logs: What a felled tree leaves and what it takes to break up (engine/trees/felling.h). A trunk's health is health_per_m3 of its own wood, never under min_health, and chop_damage is what one swing of the reference axe takes off it -- a tool does its own `damage` instead. A whole log breaks at split_at along its length into two halves; a half breaks into `billets`, short rounds of firewood that E picks up for wood_per_m3 of their own volume (at least one each). A tree that lands on another does it impact_per_chop joules' worth of chopping per chop_damage, from half its mass times the speed where it struck, above impact_min_speed; the faller keeps impact_keep of its speed afterwards, so a big one can carry on through a second tree. A log keeps its crown all the way down and sheds it once it has come to rest (or after shed_after_s), as debris_pieces clumps thrown at debris_toss of the speed they had, which fall, settle, lie there debris_rest_s and fade over debris_fade_s.
